reason: Revert changes is a button that appears in the toolbar and the filter panel when a saved view is edited. The ax probe shows button "Revert changes" with a name, so it is a control a screen-reader user finds by navigating, not a message about the result of the amount filter. The unannounced result of the filter change is the transaction count, covered by its own finding.
criterionAnalysis: 4.1.3 covers messages about success, results, waiting, progress or errors. A newly shown button is a control, not a message, and is named and focusable under 4.1.2. 1.3.1 and 2.4.3 are not affected by it appearing. No other A or AA criterion fails.

reason: Reproduced live: replaying the amount hop from transactions.filter-amount with a mutation observer, the count changed from 68 to 55 Transactions in the footer with no aria-live, status or alert ancestor, and focus stayed in the amount textbox. This is a result count, so 4.1.3 applies. The table is a polite live region (aria-live=polite, aria-busy) that announces the new rows, so users still hear the results, and the task stays possible; the missing count is friction.

Reproduced live: after the amount hop the panel title text changed to Monthly money out (edited) with no live-region ancestor while focus stayed in the textbox. The change tells the user the saved view now differs from the saved version, which is a result of the filter edit, so 4.1.3 applies. The same state is exposed on the chip (menuitem named Editing Monthly money out) and through the Save and Revert changes buttons, so this is minor friction.

Editing is a visually hidden prefix inside the saved-view chip button. It makes the chip's accessible name Editing Monthly money out (ax probe on the chip), so it is part of a control's name and not a message. The same information, that the view was edited, reaches users as the visible (edited) title, covered by its own finding.
